rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Residential rental property owners may not use algorithmic revenue management software that collects or processes competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rents. Software providers and other coordinators may not use such software to facilitate agreements or coordinate pricing among competing residential landlords.
rules.penalty: Attorney general must establish a complaint portal for alleged violations; existing remedies under the New Jersey Antitrust Act are preserved.
rules.status_basis: Signed July 20 (2026); article states the act takes effect on July 1, 2027.

requires.name: residential_rental_property
requires.text: residential rental property owners, and coordinators operating algorithmic revenue management software using nonpublic, competitively sensitive information from multiple residential rental property owners

exempt_if.name: excluded_technologies
exempt_if.text: The act does not prohibit the use of certain technologies, including spreadsheets requiring human analysis, publicly available rent estimation tools, traditional real estate listing databases, and government-administered affordable housing programs.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental property owners and coordinators using algorithmic revenue management software with nonpublic competitor data.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Spreadsheets requiring human analysis, public rent estimation tools, traditional listing databases, and government-administered affordable housing programs are not prohibited.

rules.quoted_span: The FAIR Act prohibits residential rental property owners from using algorithmic revenue management software that collects or processes competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rental prices. It also prohibits software providers and other "coordinators" from using such software to facilitate agreements or coordinate pricing among competing residential landlords.
